title: C++
subtitle: ActiveKV's runtime is C++ throughout, ported from Python under bitwise-parity gates, and the Inference Fabric's TensorRT boundary is C++.

stats.label: lines of non-test C++ in ActiveKV's engine, across 361 source files
lines in the per-step layer that prepares, binds, transfers and completes each step
lines of C++ at the Inference Fabric's TensorRT boundary

lede: ActiveKV began as Python inside vLLM. That was the right way to find out whether keeping attention history in host RAM worked, and the wrong way to ship it: the per-token path was slow, and the product logic sat in readable source. I decided to move the whole runtime to C++ with bit-identical output as the gate. The result is a C++ execution engine that loads as the vLLM plugin entry point and binds to Python through pybind11 and PyTorch's ATen. The hard problems are lifecycle problems under asynchronous DMA: staging regions are fence-protected leases with generation counters, and a fence whose outcome is unknown is quarantined and never reused. The release payload holds no Python of mine.
quote: Every optimisation waited until parity held, because a port that changes behaviour and speed at once cannot be trusted for either.
evidence: C++ and native ports with parity proof: an inference engine extension moved from Python to 77,600 lines of non-test C++ across 361 source files, with 568 test files and bit-identical output as the gate.
Native memory and lifecycle engineering: fence-protected staging leases with generation counters under asynchronous DMA, a fence of unknown outcome quarantined and never reused.
TensorRT and TensorRT-LLM engineering: a 9,500-line C++ layer at the TensorRT boundary that allows no device allocation after warm-up and rejects compute-stream synchronisation at run time.
author: Corey James
